items.stem: An employee alleges harassment by a supervisor. What is the most defensible first HR action?

options.text: Begin a prompt, impartial investigation and document each step
options.rationale: Correct: a prompt, impartial, documented investigation is the defensible first action.
Terminating before investigating creates legal risk and skips due process.

options.text: Ask the complainant to resolve it informally first
options.rationale: Pushing informal resolution can be seen as discouraging a complaint.

options.text: Wait for a written complaint before acting
options.rationale: Delaying action pending paperwork breaches the duty to respond promptly.

items.explanation: A prompt, impartial, documented investigation is the defensible first action.

options.text: New hires earn close to or more than longer-tenured staff in similar roles
options.rationale: Correct: compression is the narrowing of pay differences between new and tenured employees.
A freeze is a separate action, not the definition of compression.

options.text: Benefits costs rise faster than wages
options.rationale: That describes benefit inflation, not pay compression.
High overtime is unrelated to the compression concept.

items.explanation: Compression is the narrowing of pay between new and tenured staff.

items.stem: HR must improve the quality of a talent-acquisition pipeline. Select TWO metrics that best measure hiring quality rather than speed.

options.rationale: Correct: retention of new hires is a direct quality-of-hire signal.
Correct: hiring-manager satisfaction reflects fit and quality.
Application volume is a top-of-funnel count, not quality.

items.explanation: New-hire retention and hiring-manager satisfaction both measure quality of hire.
